claims.text: The fund offers up to £500,000.
The research should address priority questions outlined in the Strategic Review.
The aim is to improve lives in the UK.
There are two application deadlines a year: Spring and Autumn.
The outline application deadline is 5 October 2026.
In special cases, applications for up to £750,000 are accepted by prior agreement.
Most awarded grants are below £300,000.
Proposals must address one or more of the five priority questions.
The research must be relevant to at least one of the priority questions.
There must be a clear path for the research to make a difference to people’s lives.
The proposal must have a clear conceptual framework.
The research methodology must be appropriate and rigorous.
The team must have appropriate experience, expertise, and potential.
The budget requested must be appropriate and offer good value for money.
Individuals without formal employment or contractual relationship with the host institution for the project duration are not funded.
Projects led by individuals unaffiliated to any organization are not funded.
Projects led by schools or further education colleges are not funded.
Projects led by undergraduates or master’s students are not funded.
PhD fees or projects where the main purpose is to support a PhD are not funded.
The establishment of academic posts is not funded.
Ongoing costs or costs of rolling out existing work/services are not funded unless explicitly agreed in advance.
Dissemination-only projects, including campaigning work not connected to funded work, are not funded.
Local charities, replacement for statutory funding, or local social services/welfare provision are not funded.
Requests for financial help or educational fees from/on behalf of individuals are not funded.
Projects led by organizations or institutions not based in the UK are not funded.
Overseas organizations may be accepted in exceptional cases if no UK-based host is feasible, requiring strong plans for UK-focused dissemination, engagement, and impact.
